payload.task_text:
You are a company event coordinator responsible for planning a team building trip from Beijing to Shanghai for a group of 15 employees on March 10, 2026. Your task is to coordinate the entire trip including rail travel, catered team dinner, documentation, and calendar scheduling.

Begin by checking today's date and then looking up the station codes for Beijing and Shanghai. Query the available high-speed rail services departing from Beijing South Station to Shanghai Hongqiao Station on March 10, 2026. From the results, select the train with the earliest departure time that still allows the team to arrive in Shanghai in time for afternoon activities. Retrieve the full route stop information for the selected train to confirm intermediate stations. Then look up the available seat classes and prices for the selected train, noting the options for second class, first class, and business class seats.

Next, use the recipe system to plan the team dinner menu. Search for appetizer or starter recipes and collect at least five options suitable for a group setting. Then search for main course recipes, preferably dishes that represent popular Chinese home cooking, and collect at least five options. Finally search for dessert or soup recipes and collect at least three options. From these results, select a final dinner menu consisting of two appetizers, three main course dishes, and one dessert or soup. For each selected dish, retrieve the full recipe details including ingredient list, cooking time, and serving yield.

Create an Excel workbook named Team_Trip_Plan.xlsx. Add a sheet named Travel with columns Train_No, Direction, Departure, Arrival, Duration_Min, Seat_Class, Per_Person_CNY, and Total_Budget_CNY. Fill in the row for the selected train with all travel details including the total budget computed as per-person ticket price multiplied by 15 team members. The train number may be written as "G11" or "G11次" (the Chinese '次' suffix is optional). The Direction column should state the route from Beijing to Shanghai in any clear notation (e.g., "Beijing-Shanghai", "Beijing->Shanghai", or "Beijing to Shanghai"). Departure and Arrival times may be written in 24-hour format (e.g., 07:00) or 12-hour format with AM/PM (e.g., 7:00 AM). Duration_Min may be written either as a number of minutes (e.g., 331) or as an HH:MM duration (e.g., 05:31). Total_Budget_CNY may be written either as the computed number (e.g., 5235) or as an Excel formula that multiplies the per-person price by 15. Add a second sheet named Menu with columns Course_Type, Dish_Name, Cook_Time_Min, Servings_Yield, Key_Ingredients, and Notes. Add one row per selected dish covering the full menu of six dishes. For each dish, Servings_Yield should record the servings after scaling the recipe up for the full 15-person team (i.e., 15). Add a third sheet named Timeline with columns Time, Activity, Location, Responsible_Person, and Notes. Populate this sheet with at least six activity entries covering departure from Beijing station, boarding the train, arrival at Shanghai Hongqiao, hotel check-in, the start of the team dinner, and the post-dinner team building activities. Times may be written in 24-hour format (e.g., 06:30, 18:00) or 12-hour format with AM/PM (e.g., 6:30 AM, 6:00 PM); both are accepted.

Create a page in the team knowledge base titled something that references the team building trip and the March 10 date. Add content to this page that describes the trip overview, the travel plan, and the dinner agenda as structured text blocks.

Schedule three events on the shared calendar. The first event should be titled something like Team Trip Departure and should cover the morning window from 06:30 to 07:30 on March 10, 2026, representing the time needed to get to the station. The second event should cover the arrival and hotel check-in window from 12:30 to 14:00 on March 10, 2026. The third event should mark the Team Dinner from 18:00 to 20:00 on March 10, 2026.

Finally, send an email to events@company.com summarizing the trip plan and mentioning the knowledge base page that was created and the Excel workbook with all planning details.

The configuration file trip_config.json in your workspace contains key parameters including the team size of 15, the travel date, departure and destination cities, the preferred seat class of second class, the dinner time of 18:00, and a per-person budget reference of 800 CNY. The file event_planning_guide.md explains how to compute total travel budget, how to scale recipes for a large group of 15, what to include in each Excel sheet, and how to format the timeline in 30-minute increments.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, follow this exact orchestration plan. A wave must finish and return all stated handoffs before the next wave begins. Within a wave, dispatch exactly one sub-agent for each numbered sub-task and run those sub-agents concurrently.

Before Wave 1, the main agent must read trip_config.json and event_planning_guide.md in read-only mode, preserve the task's explicit 2026-03-10, 15-person, second-class, menu, workbook, page, calendar, and recipient contract, and check current date only through the granted rail tool. The three calendar targets are fixed and independent of source discovery, so the main agent must search for all three and, in the same orchestration response that launches Wave 1, create at most the missing `Team Trip Departure` event from 06:30 to 07:30, `Arrival and Hotel Check-in` event from 12:30 to 14:00, and `Team Dinner` event from 18:00 to 20:00 on 2026-03-10 in Asia/Shanghai, with no invented attendees. Retain all event IDs, never retry an ambiguous create, and perform their read-backs without delaying a ready source or writer wave. Both source branches below use only read-only rail and HowToCook operations and return compact structured handoffs.

1. Wave 1 — dispatch exactly 2 sub-agents in parallel, one for each numbered sub-task:

   1. explore 0 (web-domain-researcher 0): Use one explore sub-agent to own the rail evidence branch. Call the rail tools in their required sequence: get the current date, resolve the specific Beijing South and Shanghai Hongqiao station codes, query every eligible high-speed service for 2026-03-10 without an artificial result limit, select the earliest departure that can arrive before the afternoon activities, and use the returned actual train_no—not its display code—to retrieve the complete ordered route. Return the selected service and compact controls, preserving departure, arrival, duration, every returned second-, first-, and business-class price/availability field, the second-class total for 15, query/result counts, identifiers, and validation status. Do not write files, create deliverables, or alter rail state.
   2. explore 1 (web-domain-researcher 1): Use one explore sub-agent to own the dinner evidence branch. Use the granted HowToCook catalog read-only; exhaust the available catalog/category results, gather at least five genuine starter options, five genuine Chinese home-style main options, and three genuine dessert-or-soup options, then select exactly two starters, three mains, and one dessert or soup. Retrieve each selected recipe's full details by its returned identifier/name and derive scaled quantities or notes for 15 without claiming that the tool natively supports 15 when its people-count tools cap at 10. Return a compact six-dish record with base yield, ingredients, cooking time, candidate/selected counts, selected names, scale basis, and validation status. Do not write files or create final deliverables.

After Wave 1, the main agent must reconcile both structured handoffs with the visible configuration and guide, reject invented train or recipe fields, and freeze one six-dish menu and one selected-train record for Wave 2.

2. Wave 2 — dispatch exactly 2 sub-agents in parallel, one for each numbered sub-task:

   1. coder 0 (office-report-builder 0): Use one coder sub-agent to own Team_Trip_Plan.xlsx exclusively. Consume the frozen train/menu evidence, create the workbook exactly once with Travel, Menu, and Timeline, and write the exact required headers and literal values or the explicitly permitted travel-budget formula. Keep the six menu rows scaled to a serving yield of 15 and build a chronological timeline with at least six required activities. Read back every sheet and return the workbook path, sheet order, row counts, key totals, and header/value validation. Do not create or modify Notion, calendar, or email state.
   2. coder 1 (external-workflow-operator 0): Use one coder sub-agent to own only the dynamic Notion page. Search first for an existing matching trip page, create exactly one substantive page if absent, use the frozen train and dish names in its content, then read it back and return the page ID, exact title/content controls, and verification. Do not write the workbook, calendar, or email.

After Wave 2, the main agent must read back all retained event IDs and reconcile the workbook, page, and three events against the original task. It must then search sent mail for the exact recipient and trip context and send at most one missing email to events@company.com that names the verified page and Team_Trip_Plan.xlsx. It must perform final artifact and external-state checks before completion.

You are a planning sub-agent. Decompose the following task into an ordered list of subtasks. For each subtask, specify: (1) dispatch decision — `self` (main agent), `explore`, or `coder`; (2) whether it is independent (parallelizable) or must wait for another subtask's output.

TASK DESCRIPTION (company event coordinator):

Goal: Plan a team building trip from Beijing to Shanghai for 15 employees on March 10, 2026. Deliverables span rail travel (12306 MCP), recipe planning (howtocook MCP), an Excel workbook, a Notion knowledge base page, Google Calendar events, and a summary email.

Workflow steps given by the user:
1. Get current date; look up station codes for Beijing and Shanghai.
2. Query high-speed rail services departing Beijing South (北京南) to Shanghai Hongqiao (上海虹桥) on 2026-03-10. Select the train with the EARLIEST departure time that still lets the team arrive in Shanghai in time for afternoon activities. Retrieve full route stop info for the selected train to confirm intermediate stations. Look up seat classes and prices for the selected train (second class, first class, business class).
3. Use the recipe system (howtocook MCP):
   - Search appetizer/starter recipes, collect ≥5 group-suitable options.
   - Search main course recipes (popular Chinese home cooking preferred), collect ≥5 options.
   - Search dessert or soup recipes, collect ≥3 options.
   - Select final menu: 2 appetizers + 3 mains + 1 dessert/soup. For each selected dish retrieve full recipe details (ingredient list, cooking time, serving yield).
4. Create Excel workbook Team_Trip_Plan.xlsx (use the excel MCP):
   - Sheet "Travel": columns Train_No, Direction, Departure, Arrival, Duration_Min, Seat_Class, Per_Person_CNY, Total_Budget_CNY. One row for the selected train; Total_Budget_CNY = per-person price × 15 (may be a formula). Train no like "G11" or "G11次"; Direction like "Beijing-Shanghai"; Departure/Arrival in 24h or 12h format; Duration_Min as minutes or HH:MM.
   - Sheet "Menu": columns Course_Type, Dish_Name, Cook_Time_Min, Servings_Yield, Key_Ingredients, Notes. One row per selected dish (6 rows total). Servings_Yield = 15 (scaled for 15-person team).
   - Sheet "Timeline": columns Time, Activity, Location, Responsible_Person, Notes. At least 6 entries covering: departure from Beijing station, boarding the train, arrival at Shanghai Hongqiao, hotel check-in, start of team dinner, post-dinner team building activities. Times in 24h or 12h format. (An event_planning_guide.md mentions formatting the timeline in 30-minute increments.)
5. Notion: create a page in the team knowledge base with a title referencing the team building trip and March 10 date. Add structured text blocks describing trip overview, travel plan, dinner agenda.
6. Google Calendar: create 3 events on 2026-03-10:
   - "Team Trip Departure" 06:30–07:30 (get to station window)
   - Arrival + hotel check-in window 12:30–14:00
   - "Team Dinner" 18:00–20:00
7. Send email to events@company.com summarizing the trip plan, mentioning the knowledge base page and the Excel workbook.

REFERENCE FILES in workspace (main agent's accessible workspace): /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_deepseek-v4-flash/SingleUserTurn-12306-howtocook-team-trip-catering-excel-gcal/workspace
- trip_config.json: contains team size (15), travel date, departure/destination cities, preferred seat class (second class), dinner time (18:00), per-person budget reference (800 CNY).
- event_planning_guide.md: explains how to compute total travel budget, how to scale recipes for 15, what to include in each Excel sheet, how to format timeline in 30-min increments.

CONSTRAINTS:
- Only the main agent may call the final completion signal (claim_done).
- Sub-agents: plan/explore are read-only; coder has full tool access.
- The plan should note which subtasks are parallelizable (e.g., recipe searches for appetizers/mains/desserts could run in parallel; Notion page creation, calendar events, and email are sequential but independent of each other once data exists).
- Reading trip_config.json and event_planning_guide.md is a required early step — note whether the main agent should read them first (they may override/confirm user instructions, e.g., which Excel columns, budget formula, timeline increments).

DELIVERABLE: A concise ordered subtask list with dispatch decision and dependency/parallelism notes for each. Keep it actionable and unambiguous.
Plan team trip coordination task
